caption: Your PS5 already sends this. Nothing was reading it.
sub: Hungaroring, the closing stint, P4. Every number on this screen arrived over UDP from the game and was computed on this PC.

caption: Hards past twenty laps old, about half worn
sub: Wear and temperature per corner, degradation measured over your own laps — not a lookup table.

caption: Antonelli is three seconds back on tyres thirteen laps fresher
sub: Quicker now, degrading faster. All twenty cars are read from the same packets, so a question about a rival is answered with that rival's data.

caption: Box and lose the place, or stay out and defend?
sub: A stop costs 20.5 seconds. A second dry compound is mandatory here, and the engine enforces the rule rather than assuming it.

caption: Plans ranked by where they finish, not by elapsed time
sub: Compounds, box lap, projected finish, points, P75 race time and worst-case wear — for every plan it will actually let you take.

caption: The maths is deterministic. The model only reads it out.
sub: Strategy, tyre and corner analysis are computed locally in ordinary code. A language model is never handed raw telemetry to interpret.

caption: Your Pit Box — a race engineer for F1 on PS5 and PC
sub: The race here is synthetic, generated as genuine 2026-format packets; the software reading them is not. $20 once, no subscription — yourpitbox.com
